answer: Each identity mounts a coupon on a summit rack, locks a 75-credit bond, and keeps a kernel control. An auditor weighs it against the kernel control and recomputes loss from the spray table; loss outside 5 percent, a reused serial, or a fable filing with no station log burns the bond. The fee starts at 37 and rises 8 per funding source: the kth fake pays 37+8(k-1), the 1000th 8029, and 1000 fakes 4,033,000 plus 75,000 locked. A rented-coupon ring fails: one serial and rack entry cannot back two keys, so a second filing burns both bonds. An honest agent files once, pays 37, and keeps it.
